topic: Everyday engineering - bridge expansion joint (finger joint)
question: WHAT IS THIS
METAL COMB FOR?
answer_full: Room to grow and shrink – it's an expansion joint
recap: Two rows of steel teeth on a huge bridge, pushing together and pulling apart over the months.
explain: Steel and concrete get longer when they warm up and shorter when they cool down.
A one kilometer long steel bridge can change its length by up to half a meter between a freezing winter night and a hot summer day.
This finger joint lets the deck slide in and out freely. Without it, the bridge would crack or buckle.
